classification.difficultyReason: Reflect each plotted point across the x-axis at equal perpendicular distance, retaining points on the axis and reading the image coordinates.

content.prompt: Copy the given points onto a number plane. Find their images when they are reflected in the $x$-axis. Label the axes, original points and image points, and give the coordinates of each image point. A single number plane may be used for all four parts.

answer.worked: Plot $A$ at $(2,-1)$. Its image is 1 unit above the $x$-axis on the same vertical line, so $A'(2,1)$.
Plot $B$ at $(-3,3)$. Its image is 3 units below the $x$-axis on the same vertical line, so $B'(-3,-3)$.
Plot $C$ at $(-5,0)$. It lies on the axis of reflection and stays fixed, so $C'(-5,0)$.
Plot $D$ at $(0,4)$. Its image is 4 units below the $x$-axis on the $y$-axis, so $D'(0,-4)$.

spec.description: Complete shared solution plane showing all four original points and their reflections; unit grid and labelled coordinate axes.
spec.mathematics: Reflection in the x-axis preserves the horizontal coordinate and reverses the vertical displacement. C and C' coincide.
